text.tspan: From the fasting ladder in Al-Morabbi's “Family Ramadan”
Children fasting safely
Children fasting safely
When to ask the doctor first, and when to break the fast
at once
Doctor first:
With diabetes or any chronic illness, or a medicine taken
regularly during the day.
Also:
Being very underweight or slow growth, or a recent illness such
as fever, diarrhoea or vomiting.
Stop signs:
Dizziness, paleness or a cold sweat; a severe headache;
vomiting; very little or very dark urine.
When a sign appears:
He breaks the fast at once with water and a
date or juice, then rests. No blame, no comparison.
Suhoor:
Water plus slow-digesting food: wholemeal bread, oats,
eggs, yoghurt. Not sweets on their own.
Water little and often:
From iftar to bedtime, not a large amount all
at once.
The program's rule
No fasting before seven, and breaking the fast when tired is not failure.
Fainting, a seizure, confusion or difficulty waking: call an ambulance at once.
